messages.content: The Santa Fe org can pick me up Wednesday morning, and the Albuquerque library confirmed 3:00 p.m. Can you rerun the lodging choice? I’m comparing two nights in Santa Fe versus one Santa Fe night and one Albuquerque airport night. Please include tax plus likely shuttle/rideshare costs, and check breakfast, room coffee/fridge, and dinner options.
Yes. Should I keep Old Santa Fe Inn as the Santa Fe option and use the Hampton near ABQ airport you found, or do you want downtown Albuquerque still in the mix?
Use Old Santa Fe Inn and the airport Hampton at $158 refundable. Downtown can be backup if you think the airport is a mistake.

Here is the cleaner comparison using estimated tax and car-free transfers. Staff pickup is treated as no cost.

Option | Est. hotel after tax | Likely ground | Est. total | Practical notes
Both nights Santa Fe, Old Santa Fe Inn | about $484 | $165-$225 | $649-$709 | Easy Plaza dinners and no hotel change, but you must go Santa Fe-ABQ Wednesday, return to Santa Fe that night, then leave early again Thursday. Highest transfer risk. Breakfast listed; room coffee and mini-fridge appear listed but should be confirmed.
Split: Tue Old Santa Fe Inn, Wed Hampton ABQ airport | about $425 | $115-$155 | $540-$580 | Hotel change, but Wednesday night puts you near ABQ for the Thursday debrief and flight. Breakfast at both; Hampton lists in-room coffee and mini-fridge. Dinner is less charming than the Plaza, but manageable by nearby restaurant or short rideshare.

My recommendation is the split stay. It is cheaper after ground cost and much lower-risk on Thursday.
Walk me through Wednesday and Thursday. They can pick me up at 8:45 from the Plaza and drop me at the depot around noon.

Wednesday works if the depot drop is firm: 8:45 pickup, Santa Fe visit roughly 9:00-11:30, drop at depot around 12:05, southbound Rail Runner or shuttle around 12:30-12:45, Albuquerque arrival around 2:10-2:25, then a short rideshare to the library. That gives roughly 30 minutes before the 3:00 meeting. Afterward, rideshare to the airport Hampton and check in.\n\nThursday is easier from the airport hotel: rideshare to the 10:30 debrief, finish 12:15, lunch downtown if you keep it quick, then ride back toward the hotel/airport with plenty of margin for a midafternoon flight.
If I stay in Santa Fe both nights, is Thursday actually doable or just technically possible?

Technically possible, but fragile. You would need an early Santa Fe departure, carry luggage through the morning, and any shuttle/train delay would eat into the 10:30 debrief. It also adds a second north-south transfer after the Wednesday library meeting. I would not choose that unless the Albuquerque hotel fell through.
Can you double-check the Hampton basics? I don’t want lobby-only coffee or breakfast that turns out to be a paid buffet.

The Hampton airport listing shows free hot breakfast and standard rooms with a coffee/tea maker plus mini-fridge. I would still call or message for written confirmation because airport properties sometimes vary by room type. Old Santa Fe Inn also lists included breakfast and room coffee/fridge details. Dinner: Old Santa Fe is much better for walkable restaurants Tuesday; Hampton is acceptable Wednesday, with nearby casual options and easy delivery/rideshare, but not a destination neighborhood.
So airport Hampton over downtown Homewood for Wednesday night?

For this agenda, yes by a small margin. Downtown Homewood is closer to the library/debrief, but the Hampton makes luggage and the Thursday airport transfer simpler and is cheaper on the current rate. Hold the Hampton refundable, keep the second Santa Fe night only until the Wednesday southbound transfer is confirmed, and confirm these four items before canceling anything: staff pickup/drop time in writing, exact Rail Runner or shuttle time, Hampton breakfast/coffee/mini-fridge, and luggage plan if you go straight from Thursday lunch to ABQ.

messages.content: I have the refundable hotel holds now. Can you refresh ORD to Albuquerque for Oct. 14-16? Thursday debrief is 10:30 to 12:15 downtown, so I want lunch and a calm ride to ABQ before returning. United is fine if it lines up, but timing matters more.

Best current fits, all times local and economy fares before bags/seat fees:

Option | Outbound Tue | Return Thu | Fare | Read
American via DFW | ORD 8:05 a.m. -> ABQ 12:20 p.m. | ABQ 3:18 p.m. -> ORD 8:34 p.m. | about $438 | Best balance. Good Tuesday arrival for the Santa Fe shuttle and a workable Thursday return.
United via DEN | ORD 8:45 a.m. -> ABQ 12:58 p.m. | ABQ 3:35 p.m. -> ORD 8:58 p.m. | about $487 | Also workable, but costs more and arrives a bit later both ways.
Cheaper late return | similar midday ABQ arrival | ABQ about 5:50 p.m. -> ORD about 11:15 p.m. | about $356 | Saves money but makes for a long connection and late Chicago arrival.

I would ticket the American midafternoon return if the fare is still near $438.
Is 3:18 too tight if the debrief ends at 12:15 and I want to eat something?

It is not too tight if lunch stays simple. A safe version is: debrief ends 12:15, quick lunch downtown until about 12:55, rideshare by 1:00, reach the airport area around 1:20-1:30, and be inside ABQ by about 1:40. That is comfortable for a 3:18 departure with a carry-on. If lunch slips past 1:10, skip the hotel stop and go straight to the airport.
How much am I paying to avoid the late return?

About $82 over the late-return option. In exchange, you avoid getting back to Chicago around 11:15 p.m., reduce connection fatigue, and keep the day from stretching after two site-visit mornings. I think the $82 is worth it unless reimbursement is pushing hard on the fare.
And the United option is not worth the extra $49?

Not on these timings. It is a perfectly acceptable itinerary, but it is $49 more, gets you to Albuquerque later on Tuesday, and gets you home a little later Thursday. If the American fare jumps or United drops within about $15-$20, I would reconsider; at the current spread, American is the cleaner buy.
Okay. Give me the ticketing note.

Ticket American ORD-ABQ for Oct. 14-16: outbound Tuesday around 8:05 a.m. via DFW, arriving ABQ about 12:20 p.m.; return Thursday around 3:18 p.m. via DFW, arriving ORD about 8:34 p.m. Save the fare basis and change rules, then match the Tuesday ABQ arrival to the Santa Fe shuttle pickup and keep the Thursday lunch plan capped at about 45 minutes.

messages.content: Switching to the Minneapolis arts data conference, Nov. 12-14. I present Thursday morning and need to arrive Wednesday for an organizer meeting. The block is at the meeting hotel, but a nearby limited-service hotel is cheaper and includes breakfast. Can you compare flight-and-hotel pairings with totals, transfers, meeting convenience, breakfast, room coffee/fridge, and dinner access?
Yes. What time is the Wednesday organizer meeting, and when does the Friday closing lunch end? Also, is there a nightly rate guideline I should keep in mind?

Organizer meeting is 2:45 Wednesday at the conference hotel. Closing lunch should end 1:15 Friday. Under $225 before tax is easier, but the event hotel can be justified if the total difference is reasonable. Use ORD unless MDW is a lot better.
Got it. I will keep arrivals before noon Wednesday and returns after 3:00 Friday. Are the hotels Hyatt Regency Minneapolis for the block and Hampton Inn & Suites Downtown for the lower-cost option?
Yes. Add Home2 Downtown if it has a real kitchenette, but keep the comparison to three choices.

Here are the best pairings I would compare. Totals estimate airfare + two hotel nights with tax + airport rideshare; meals are excluded except where breakfast is included.

Pairing | Timing | Hotel and amenities | Est. total | Trade-off
United + Hyatt Regency block | ORD 10:10 a.m. -> MSP 11:42 a.m.; Fri MSP 3:35 p.m. -> ORD 5:05 p.m. | Block hotel, about $239 before tax. Breakfast not included. Standard rooms list coffee maker and mini-fridge; on-site restaurant/cafe. | about $868, plus breakfast if not conference-provided | Easiest for presenting and no weather commute. Highest hotel cost but easiest to justify as event hotel.
United + Hampton Downtown | Same United flights | About $176 before tax. Free breakfast; room coffee maker and mini-fridge listed. About 0.4 miles from conference hotel. | about $742 if mostly walking, about $765 with a couple short rideshares | Strong value and breakfast included, but cold-weather walk or short ride to sessions.
Delta + Home2 Downtown | ORD 9:25 a.m. -> MSP 10:57 a.m.; Fri MSP 4:05 p.m. -> ORD 5:42 p.m. | About $169 before tax. Free breakfast; kitchenette-style room with fridge, microwave, coffee setup. Farther walk, roughly 0.6-0.7 miles. | about $730-$755 depending on local rides | Cheapest practical setup and best Friday cushion, but least convenient for a Thursday presentation.
Does that United arrival give enough room before 2:45 without renting a car?

Yes. If you land at 11:42, a rideshare should put you downtown around 12:25-12:40 in normal conditions. That leaves time for lunch, check-in if the room is ready, or luggage drop before the 2:45 organizer meeting. Light rail is cheaper but closer to 40-45 minutes with luggage, so I would use rideshare on arrival.
I am really deciding whether the block convenience is worth about $125. I present at 9:15 Thursday.

For a 9:15 presentation, the block has real value. You avoid walking or waiting for a rideshare with a laptop, coat, and materials; you can do an AV check and still get back to your room; and weather becomes irrelevant. The Hampton savings are real, especially with breakfast included, but after adding a couple of local rideshares the net savings may be closer to $90-$110.
What about breakfast at Hyatt? And please verify the coffee and fridge there.

The Hyatt block does not appear to include breakfast. The hotel has an on-site restaurant/cafe, so estimate roughly $18-$25 per morning unless the conference provides food. Standard room details list an in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge, but I would confirm those on the block reservation because conference inventory can vary.
And dinner Wednesday? I may be tired after the organizer meeting.

Hyatt is easiest: on-site dining plus several Nicollet/downtown options nearby. Hampton is still fine, with casual downtown restaurants within a short walk, but it is less appealing if it is icy or windy. Home2 is workable for delivery or a quick nearby meal, but it does not win on dinner convenience.
If I choose Hampton, could I just rideshare Thursday morning and Friday with my materials?

Yes. Budget roughly $10-$15 each way for short downtown rides. If you rideshare Thursday morning, Thursday evening, and Friday with materials, Hampton still likely saves about $80-$100 versus Hyatt after breakfast and local rides. The risk is not cost; it is waiting on a car during the exact window you need to be calm and on time.
Is the Friday 3:35 return okay after a 1:15 closing lunch?

It is okay if lunch ends close to 1:15. Leave downtown by 1:35, arrive MSP around 2:05, and you have about 90 minutes before departure. If the closing lunch often runs long or you expect post-panel conversations, the Delta 4:05 return buys a nicer cushion for a modest fare difference.
Could you give me the final recommendation with one backup?

Recommendation: United nonstop ORD-MSP with the Hyatt Regency block. Estimated travel/lodging total is about $868 before paid breakfasts. It is the lowest-friction plan for a Wednesday organizer meeting and Thursday 9:15 presentation, and the event-hotel exception makes the $239 rate defensible. Backup: United plus Hampton Downtown at about $760-$765 if the hotel cap becomes strict; use rideshares for presentation materials or bad weather.
Okay. Before I hold the Hyatt, what should I confirm?

Confirm the block cancellation deadline, total nightly rate with taxes/fees, whether any conference breakfasts are included, in-room coffee maker and mini-fridge for the room type, early check-in or luggage storage for Wednesday, restaurant/cafe hours, and the presentation room location for Thursday. If those check out, hold Hyatt first, then ticket the United flights if the fare is still close to the current quote.
